headline: Nifty FMCG index drops 6% as festive demand outlook remains key
summary: The Nifty FMCG index has declined 6% over the past six months amid cooling demand trends. Analysts are now looking toward the upcoming festive season to potentially trigger a recovery in volume growth. Marico, Hindustan Unilever, and Tata Consumer Products are being highlighted as key stocks to watch for potential upside. Retail investors should note that sector performance remains heavily dependent on rural consumption recovery and festive spending patterns.
whats_next: Q2 earnings and festive season sales data
why_it_matters: Festive sales may dictate short-term returns for consumer goods portfolios.

headline: HUL Q3 preview points to higher margins and profit growth
hook: Profit growth expected despite ice-cream demerger impact
summary: Hindustan Unilever's upcoming Q3 results are projected to show margins rising to 24.8% alongside a PAT increase of nearly 18%. This performance comes amid the operational impact of the company's ice-cream demerger process. Retail investors in the FMCG sector should monitor these earnings for demand recovery signals in rural and urban markets. The reported estimates set expectations ahead of the official financial filing.
why_it_matters: HUL earnings set the tone for the Indian FMCG sector.
winners_losers: HUL holders gain / FMCG peers watched

headline: PB Fintech, Wipro and six other BSE 100 stocks hit 52-week lows
hook: Eight major index stocks hit annual lows
summary: Eight BSE 100 constituents, including PB Fintech, Wipro, Havells India, Britannia Industries, Tata Consumer Products, Godrej Consumer Products, Hindustan Unilever, and ONGC, hit fresh 52-week lows, with some slipping up to 45% in a month. This occurred as the Sensex fell 49 points to settle at 72,480. These declines reflect broader downward pressure on large-cap Indian equities. Retail investors holding these prominent stocks face significant near-term capital erosion.
why_it_matters: Your large-cap holdings may be seeing sharp short-term corrections.
